title: Org & Team Settings — Access Surface Mapping + Wireframe Notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc to align the org/team settings access surface for the console. Focus: unify RBAC controls, API key and service account lifecycle, and a usable audit log surface for both admins and delegated team leads. Goal is to produce a single-page-ish admin view with targeted drilldowns, consistent affordances across org/team boundaries, and clear accident-prevention patterns for key material (api keys, service account secrets).

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: org-level settings + team-level settings pages, role management UI, API key manager, service account creation/rotation flow, audit view with filters and quick actions.
- Non-goal: full billing UX, identity provider setup (handled in security team), or audit ingestion pipeline.

Personas:
- Org Admin (primary): needs global/tenant-level controls, user invite, org-wide RBAC and audit.
- Team Admin / Team Lead: needs scoped RBAC, create service accounts for infra, issue API keys for devs, view team-level audit.
- SRE / Infra Owner: needs service-account-heavy flows + key rotation timelines.
- Auditor / Compliance: read-only access to audit history with good filtering and exports.

High-level principles:
1) Single surface for access decisions — show "effective permission" when viewing a principal.
2) Explicit state for secrets — never show secret material after creation; copy/retain warnings.
3) Progressive disclosure — summary table with quick actions, expand for details.
4) Safe defaults — least privilege templates for common roles, prominent revoke/rotation CTA, confirmable destructive actions.

Flows to support (sketch-level):
A. Create team -> assign initial roles: "Create team" flow should include checkboxes to copy roles from parent org or pick templates. Wireframe: left column team metadata, middle role-assignment matrix, right column preview of "effective permissions".
B. Service account create + key provisioning: modal with name, purpose, scoping (org|team|route-level), TTL for keys, CI-friendly download step (one-shot secret sheet). Wireframe notes: show a required "acknowledge one-shot secret" checkbox before download button; include rotation schedule microcopy.
C. API key manager: list view, key types (sdk | server | limited), creation modal with optional expiry and tag fields, quick revoke in list, filter by tag or owner, bulk revoke. Visual: compact table, inline badges for expiry, owner, usage (last used).
D. Role editor: role templates + custom role editor. Editor is two-column: left permission categories (models, deployments, billing-lite, keys, audit-read), right toggles + granular row-level help. Show an "effective preview" when role is assigned to a sample user (simulate).
E. Audit log: default filter = last 7 days for the org/team scope. Columns: timestamp, actor, action, target, result, route/context, link-to-entity. Filters: actor, user type (service_account/human), action type, timeframe, affected-resource-type, success/failure. Quick actions: jump to entity, download .csv for current filter, create ticket (link to JIRA template).

Wireframe component details / microcopy ideas:
- Effective permission pill: small pill that displays granted/denied with hover for "why" (shows where permission came from: role, inherited, org policy).
- Danger modal copy for key display: "This key will be shown once. Store it securely. You cannot view it again." + checkbox "I have saved this key" required. Include a copy button and a small "generate new" CTA.
- Rotation CTA: "Rotate key" -> create new key, rotate clients, revoke old after X days. Offer staged rotation helper with ephemeral link for dev to test.
- Search-as-you-type in audit: tokenization for multi-terms (actor:ava, action:revoke). Show keyboard shortcut hint (/).

Edge cases and decisions to capture:
- Inheritance vs. override: team-level grant that conflicts with org deny: choose org deny precedence (safety). Note: this is a policy decision — bring to security.
- Service accounts with mixed scope (org+team): how to display effective ownership — option: show primary scope and a stacked badge for secondary.
- API key rate-limited vs. global: allow tagging keys with "quota bucket" names but actual enforcement silo handled by infra. Need API for tag->quota mapping.
- Audit retention and pagination: UI should surface retention policy and show an "older logs are archived" indicator.

Accessibility considerations:
- Ensure danger confirmations are keyboard-focus-trapped and screen-reader friendly.
- Tables must support dense mode and row selection with aria labels.
- Color usage: red only for destructive; use icon+color for state to support colorblind users.

Backlog (first-cut, prioritized):
1) (P0) Service account key creation modal + one-shot secret flow + audit event generation. Est: 8. Owners: eng + product. Linked: JIRA-PS-5423.
2) (P0) API key list + create/revoke + tags + last-used col. Est: 5. Owners: product-console.
3) (P1) Role template library + import from org templates + copy-paste share. Est: 5.
4) (P1) Effective permission pill + hover "why" micro-interaction. Est: 3.
5) (P1) Audit log quick filters + CSV export + JIRA ticket action. Est: 8.
6) (P2) Staged rotation helper (wizard) for keys. Est: 8.
7) (P2) Mobile/responsive tweaks for compact table. Est: 3.
8) (P3) Simulation sandbox "assign role to demo user" for training. Est: 5.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Time-to-issue-key (from create->copy) < 45s for 90th percentile (measured via telemetry).
- Reduction in support tickets related to key rotation by 30% after rotation helper launch.
- Audit export usage: > 50 orgs/month (initial target).
- Error rate for accidental public key leaks (post-creation delete) < 0.1% (tracked via support spike).

Open questions / risks (to review with security and infra):
- Should we allow showing 'last-used' for keys when usage is routed through proxies (privacy concern)? Security input needed.
- Policy precedence (org deny vs team grant) - confirm with legal/security.
- How long do we allow ephemeral keys to be active by default? 24 hours? 7 days?

Notes-to-self / design ideas to try in prototype:
- Try a "compact row" that expands in-place rather than separate detail page for service accounts. Fast detail: last used, attached keys, rotation CTA.
- Inline "who can see this" crumb in the header (Org / Team / Route) so users never lose context.
- Small teaching overlay on first-time user for Org Admin showing where to find revoke and audit.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Sync with security (Priya) on policy precedence and retention policy (this week).
- Mock up 3 variants of the service-account row (compact, card, modal) and test with 3 eng teams next sprint.
- Create JIRA tasks for the P0s and attach this doc + initial sketches.

Appendix: quick links / sketches placeholders:
- Sketch A: service-account-row-compact.png (placeholder)
- Sketch B: api-key-create-modal-v1.png (placeholder)
- Example copy snippet for danger modal: "This key will only be shown once. Anyone with this value can access your account. Store it securely and rotate frequently."

---
Status: draft — comments welcome. If you add images to the drive, link here and update the sketches placeholders.
